description: `cli-health` validate and search findings are exposed to `scenario-auditor` as an additional rule source, enabling cross-scenario policy enforcement without duplicating validation logic.

requirements.description: The structured findings produced by `cli-health validate` and `cli-health search` must be exposable to `scenario-auditor` as an additional rule source via a defined integration contract (e.g., a structured JSON findings file written to a well-known path, or a Connect-RPC endpoint on the cli-health service). The scenario-auditor must be able to consume these findings and incorporate them into cross-scenario policy enforcement without duplicating the underlying validation logic. The integration must not require scenario-auditor to invoke raw HTTP endpoints.
requirements.title: Scenario-Auditor Integration as an Additional Rule Source

validation.notes: Given a completed validate run with --output-findings=<path>, a structured JSON findings file is written to the specified path with the correct schema
Given the findings file consumed by a mock scenario-auditor rule loader, all findings are correctly parsed and typed
Given zero findings, the output findings file contains an empty findings array, not a missing file

Configure scenario-auditor to consume cli-health findings for a test scenario; run both tools and assert scenario-auditor's report includes cli-health-sourced findings without re-running validation logic
Assert that scenario-auditor's integration path does not make raw HTTP calls to cli-health (verified by network trace or mock assertion)
Cross-scenario policy enforcement is centralized in scenario-auditor; cli-health remains the single source of truth for manifest validation findings

title: Scenario-auditor rule integration
